cohort: 6822 pregnant women in New Zealand (representing 11% of all births in NZ during the recruitment period 2009-2010)
finding: The study found that multiple maternal health indicators and behaviors during pregnancy, including smoking, elevated BMI, insufficient weight gain, alcohol use, and diagnosed illness before pregnancy, were associated with increased risk of adverse birth outcomes.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was associated with having a diagnosed illness before pregnancy, elevated BMI, greater pregnancy weight gain, and less pregnancy exercise.
